data.why: Walmart's agreement to add 300 new drone delivery sites with Zipline was announced just days ago and signals massive operational expansion. For a Head of Strategic Finance, rolling out hundreds of sites creates immediate capital allocation and procurement approval friction.
data.angle: Surging procurement approvals and purchase requests across hundreds of new drone delivery site buildouts

not_chosen.reason: Bad news: headline references that Zipline nearly died two years ago.
Bad news: headline mentions a competitor stock cratering.
The $1.5B Series I round was covered across dozens of outlets, so every sales rep will lead with the funding headline.
Hiring a Strategic Finance Manager for manufacturing is relevant, but the 300-site commercial rollout is much fresher and drives the actual volume.
Headcount growth of 27% is a broad metric rather than a specific operational catalyst.
Mac has been in the role for 468 days, making the role transition too old to serve as a compelling hook.

data.subject: 300 delivery sites
data.body:
Hi Mac,

Walmart is adding 300 drone delivery sites with Zipline. Rolling out hundreds of new locations usually means a flood of purchase orders for hardware and local setups. When spend ramps up that fast, who is reviewing every request to keep budgets in line?

Amgen automated 85% of purchase requisitions through approval with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
